Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. A few quick points from the edgeops team (copied):

- Outbound NAT: we cannot open a /16 at the perimeter. We can either allow specific FQDNs (preferred) or a small range (up to /24) for scheduled model/artifact pulls.
- Ports: TCP 9001-9002 are fine to the collector IPs you listed, but we require mTLS and a cert pin for any monitoring ingestion.
- We have IPS signatures that will block long-lived plaintext streams on uncommon ports; please ensure streaming uses TLS 1.3.

I've attached our firewall requirements doc for reference. Two asks for you: 1) can you provide a v2 diagram that expresses the allowed-hostname approach as an alternative, and 2) can your team call out how the KV-cache syncs across the data plane so we can validate traffic patterns?

Samir
Network Architecture Manager, Acme Payments
samir@acmepayments.com
Attachment: acme-firewall-reqs.docx

Samir — thanks for the quick review and the policy doc. I've incorporated both suggestions into v2 (attached) and annotated two alternative patterns:

A) FQDN-first egress (preferred):
   - Redwood will attempt artifact/model pulls via hostname (models.redwood-inference.com).
   - Add mTLS enforcement at ingress, and we will support cert pinning for the collector.
   - Minimal IP footprint required: we will publish a small rotated /24 for scheduled pulls; runtime streaming will be hostname-based.

B) Fixed-IP fallback:
   - If your compliance team requires fixed IPs, we've outlined a /24 fallback for downloads and the control-plane telemetry IPs.

KV-cache / data-plane sync note (per your ask):
- KV cache sync is strictly peer-to-peer between inference worker pods inside the tenant overlay; control-plane does not carry request payloads.
- Sync traffic is initiated only on cache-miss events and is encrypted in transit (TLS). Typical flow: worker -> worker (same AZ preferred) -> fallback to inter-AZ NAT if required.
- I've called out estimated bandwidth per sync (see page 3 of the attached v2).

Next steps / action owners:
- Jordan: can you produce a short test plan (egress validation + mTLS handshake test) and a prescriptive packet-capture checklist?
- Kimberly: please confirm whether the telemetry collector can be configured for cert pinning; if not, we'll propose an alternate ingestion path.
- Marissa: will own the runbook updates and evidence artifacts for the deployment acceptance packet.

Attachments: vpc-service-boundary-v2-annotated.pdf

Best,
Priyom
